thread:
kevin: FYI - hybrid-int6 canary (sablex-hybrid) shows a weird streaming funcall failure: two JSON objects get glued together with no separator, e.g. `}{` in the middle of the NDJSON stream. Causes downstream tool runner to attempt a second toolcall unexpectedly.

yasmin: Oof. Do you have an example output?

kevin: Yep, raw assembled fragment below (we parse afterward):
```
{"tool":"fetch","args":{"q":"sales"}}{"tool":"log","args":{"level":"info"}}
```
No newline or space between the curly braces. Parser that expects single-object-per-response chokes or processes both objects leading to duplicate side effects.

ola: Is this only on hybrid-int6? Mirrors on int8/fp16?

kevin: Mirrors on fp16/int8-stable show baseline. Only the hybrid-int6 packer shows ~0.35% of calls with glued-json.

canary-bot: canary-5799999990 running on hybrid-int6-01 at 14:02 UTC. metric: glued_json_rate=0.34% (baseline 0.00%).

sam: Any correlation with kvcache or streaming resume?

kevin: Yes strong correlation: happens when prefix_cache + streaming-resume are enabled and the model emits a final '}' followed immediately by a resume of cached tokens that start with '{'. The concat code doesn't insert a newline when joining fragments in this path.

yasmin: That explains it. Our NDJSON contract is "one JSON object per line" — missing linebreak violates consumer assumptions. Short term: insert a post-assembly normalization step that ensures a single newline between adjacent JSON object boundaries. Emit telemetry `ndjson_normalized`.

ola: Agreed for mitigation. For root cause: (1) capture raw token-id traces around boundary, (2) compare byte roundtrip for hybrid-int6 vs fp16, (3) run streaming-resume with prefix_cache off to confirm.

kevin: I've started a token-id dump for 25 failing samples and kicked a prefix-off mirror.

ci-bot: CI job queued: ndjson-boundary-fuzz (inject `}{` cases and resume scenarios).

kevin: Prefix-off mirror parse_ok=99.99% -> nails prefix_cache + resume concat.

sam: Ok plan: A) add normalization layer that inserts a `\n` between `}` and `{` when they are adjacent (feature-flagged and off for canaries) (kevin), B) add unit+fuzz tests for resume+prefix concat (ola), C) bisect hybrid-int6 packer commits touching token-stream concat if normalization doesn't fully resolve (sam).

yasmin: Also be careful: we shouldn't silently modify user payloads. Normalizer should only add newline between two top-level JSON objects when the first is closed and the second starts with `{` or `[` and the first isn't a string tail. Emit `ndjson_inserted_break` telemetry with minimal context.

kevin: Good call. We'll run normalization opt-in for customers initially. For canaries we keep strict parsing to retain signal.

ola: I'll add a linter rule in the struct-output harness that fails if assembled stream contains `}{` without intervening whitespace, so CI will catch regressions.

sam: Also add a small e2e test that asserts tool-runner only processes a single object unless NDJSON contains more than one newline-separated line. We had a user-facing bug last year when double invokes happened.

kevin: Filed ML-ONBOARD-4021 and uploaded failing dumps. Pushed a draft PR for normalization behind flag.

yasmin: Thanks. If bisect shows packer emitted spurious `{` at resume start we escalate to tokenmap/packer owners.

kevin: Will keep updates here. For now enabling opt-in normalization reduced glued_json_rate to 0.01% for opted-in tenants.

ola: Nice. Follow-up: add telemetry metric `ndjson_duplicate_object_detected` and correlate with side-effectful toolcalls.

sam: I'll schedule the bisect for tomorrow across the last 6 hybrid-int6 commits that touched stream concat. Ping me if you want to pair. :thumbsup:
